messages:
alex: Heads-up — proposing a schema change for console telemetry: switch from the current envelope-per-route rows to a time-series micro-sharded table keyed by (route_tag, tenant_id, window_start). This should speed up p99 queries for dashboard rollups and make rollouts more incremental.
julia: short Q — what's route_tag vs route_id? can you show a tiny example?
alex: route_tag = stable business-facing identifier (string), route_id = internal PK. We'll keep route_id for joins but index primarily by route_tag so the UI queries are simple and stable across model versions.
mat: concern: backfill cost and some ad-hoc queries currently rely on JSONB attributes on the envelope. Also, how does this affect real-time quota checks in the API path?
priya: +1 on reindexing cost. Proposal: introduce new table route_metrics_ts, dual-write for 4-8 weeks, then backfill historical windows via a throttled job. Do we pick composite PK or surrogate with unique index?
alex: leaning composite PK to avoid extra lookups in hot paths. Example DDL snippet:
```sql
CREATE TABLE route_metrics_ts (
  route_tag TEXT,
  tenant_id UUID,
  window_start TIMESTAMP,
  tokens BIGINT,
  requests BIGINT,
  PRIMARY KEY (route_tag, tenant_id, window_start)
);
```
julia: runtime quota checks must be sub-ms. If the API needs to read route_metrics_ts synchronously, we should keep a tiny current_window cache in redis aggregated from the TS table, or a separate materialized current_window table keyed by tenant+route.
mat: console dashboards rely on historical attributes stored in envelope rows (e.g., route_metadata JSON). We should replicate necessary attrs into the TS projection to avoid expensive joins on every query.
priya: alternate: keep envelope rows immutable and add a lightweight projection table route_meta with denormalized tags. route_metrics_ts references route_meta by route_tag. Migration plan: backfill route_meta first, then populate metrics.
console-bot: CI for schema-compat tests passing on branch "route-ts-proto": https://ci.company/1234 :white_check_mark:
alex: rollout UX idea: add a feature-flag per-tenant to opt into the new TS model so customers can validate dashboards and quota behaviors. Console should surface "metrics source" and migration status per-tenant.
julia: backfill pattern suggestion (throttled windowed inserts):
```sql
INSERT INTO route_metrics_ts (route_tag, tenant_id, window_start, tokens, requests)
SELECT route_tag, tenant_id, window_start, sum(tokens), sum(requests)
FROM envelope_metrics
WHERE window_start BETWEEN $s AND $e
GROUP BY route_tag, tenant_id, window_start;
```
We run in 1h windows and cap to X inserts/sec.
mat: ingestion service should emit both shapes (envelope + ts) during canary so downstream consumers can verify without a hard cut. That reduces blast radius.
priya: rollback story: do not delete envelope rows on cutover. Keep dual-write for 90 days and a reconcile job that flags discrepancies > 1% so we can audit before trimming.
alex: action items (short):
- route_meta denorm table and projection backfill (mat)
- add dualwrite to ingestion + schema-compat tests (julia)
- windowed backfill job + throttle + monitoring (priya)
- console feature-flag UI & migration status display (assign to console team / ping ben)
- plan a staged canary on staging (30m observation) then 1% prod, 10% prod, full cutover
julia: pinging @ben-console (OOO till Tue) — Ben can own UI pieces when back. In the meantime, please add a mock Console PR so we can exercise APIs.
mat: perf sims on staging traffic show dashboard p99 drops from ~2.1s to ~350ms for most route queries after indexing and projection. I can attach the sim script later.
alex: OK I'll draft the migration runbook and schedule a 30m canary on staging next Thu 10:00. Any objections?
priya: :+1: no objections, will start the backfill scaffolding.
julia: :eyes: small nit — add a reconciliation metric to the console that shows "ts vs envelope delta" over time.
deploy-bot: scheduled deployment to staging for branch "route-ts-proto" at 2025-11-06T10:00Z
alex: I'll file the runbook doc and post the link here when done.
